question: In which year was the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) initially constituted under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister of India by an executive order?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) was initially constituted in **2005** under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister of India by an executive order.
 
• NDMA is the apex body responsible for disaster management in India, aiming to build a safe and disaster-resilient nation.
 
• It functions under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, which provides a legal framework for disaster risk reduction and response.
 
• The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NDMA, ensuring high-level leadership in disaster management efforts.
 
• NDMA's primary role includes planning, coordinating, and implementing measures for disaster prevention, preparedness, and mitigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005**

 
 
• This Act was enacted to provide a legal framework for disaster preparedness and response in India.
 
• It defines roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders, including NDMA, SDMAs (State Disaster Management Authorities), and local authorities.
 
• The Act also includes provisions for financial mechanisms like the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).
 
 
 
• **Structure of NDMA**
 
 
• The NDMA consists of a Chairperson (Prime Minister) and up to nine members, including a Vice-Chairperson.
 
• It is supported by executive committees, advisory groups, and technical experts to ensure effective decision-making.
 
 
 
• **Key Functions of NDMA**
 
 
• Formulating disaster management policies and plans.
 
• Coordinating disaster response and recovery efforts across India.
 
• Promoting community-based disaster risk reduction initiatives.
 
 
 
• **India's Disaster Management Framework**
 
 
• India follows a multi-tiered disaster management system, with NDMA at the national level, SDMAs at the state level, and District Authorities at the district level.
 
• The framework emphasizes the "Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction" guidelines for global disaster resilience.
